info.description: Web reading: the search engines asked directly, a page read as words, a link's preview, a page's markup as served, the picture at an address, the engines that answer with their standing, and a picture search whose hits carry their licence fields. No HTTP of its own: the tools are the contract, served by its MCP server and placed with a tool host, each a thin call of one function of the client this repository publishes as its Rust crate. It calls no other service. Bodies are JSON with camelCase keys; times are integers of epoch milliseconds; a failure is the error shape, its code one of bad-request, unsafe-address, not-markup, too-large, upstream-failed and failed.
info.title: bmo-explorer

x-harness.entry: A harness searches with explorer_web_search and reads a hit with explorer_web_fetch; it finds pictures with explorer_search_images and reads one with explorer_fetch_raster.

x-tools.description: Ask the search engines directly; the hits, as each engine answered them, mixed one from each engine in turn. Name the engines or their categories from explorer_search_engines, or none for the general ones.

engines.description:
The engines to ask: each an engine's name as explorer_search_engines lists it, or a category (general,
news, images, it) standing for every engine of it. An empty list asks the general engines.

limit.description: How many hits to answer, 1 to 30; 10 where absent.

x-tools.description: Ask the image search engines directly; each picture answered as fields rather than a snippet: its direct address, the page it stands on, title, creator, publisher, pixel dimensions, media type and licence. A field the source does not state is null, and no licence is inferred. Name the image engines or their categories from explorer_search_engines, or none for every image engine.
